meta.title: OpenAgenda MCP - search, edit and moderate your events from your AI assistant
meta.description: Connect OpenAgenda to your AI assistant. It searches, edits and moderates your events, with your account and your permissions.
hero.title: Search, edit and moderate your events from your AI assistant
hero.lede: Connect OpenAgenda to your assistant, such as Claude. Ask your question: it works on your agendas, with your account and your permissions.
sketch.alt: A person asks a question, the agenda answers with a list
examples.title: Just ask, it takes care of the rest
examples.label: Examples
find.ask: Which concerts are on in Nantes this week?
find.says: Here are this week's concerts in the Nantes Métropole agenda:
find.more: Also Edouard Ferlet, Lagrimas and Zamdane. Would you like me to filter by price or neighbourhood?
edit.ask: Add the events from this spreadsheet to my agenda, for moderation.
edit.says: Done: 468 events created, awaiting your moderation.
edit.point1: Locations matched with those of your agenda, or created when they were missing.
edit.point2: 20 addresses to review: geocoding could not find them, here is the list.
edit.point3: No duplicates at the next update: each event keeps the identifier from your spreadsheet.
moderate.ask: Publish the events from this spreadsheet that have an image, a location and an upcoming date.
moderate.says: Done: the complete events are published, the others remain to be checked.
moderate.point1: Published: the ones that meet your criteria.
moderate.point2: To check: the others, with what they are missing, so that you can decide.
moderate.point3: Depending on your permissions: you must be a moderator or administrator of the agenda to publish.
connect.title: Connect your assistant
connect.lede: Give this address to your assistant, then sign in with your OpenAgenda account.
connect.fast.title: With one command
connect.fast.text: For the tools installed on this computer: Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code and many others. The command lets you choose your tools and where to configure them. It requires Node.js.
connect.tools.title: Or tool by tool
connect.tools.label: Assistants
claude.step1: In Claude's settings, open Connectors, then Add custom connector.
step.signin: Sign in with your OpenAgenda account.
claude.step3: Sign in with your OpenAgenda account and accept the permissions.
chatgpt.step1: In ChatGPT's settings, turn on developer mode.
chatgpt.step2: Create a connector and paste the server address.
chatgpt.hint: Depending on your ChatGPT plan, editing and moderation may not be available.
claudecode.step2: Type {command} and sign in from your browser.
other.text: Give the server address to your client (Streamable HTTP). Sign-in uses OAuth 2.1 with your OpenAgenda account. Discovery metadata.
control.title: You stay in control
control.rights.title: Your permissions, nothing more
control.rights.text: The assistant acts with your account. It can only see and change what you can see and change.
control.isolated.title: Isolated execution
control.isolated.text: Each action runs in a sandbox that can only reach the OpenAgenda API.
control.open.title: Open code
control.open.text: The server is open source: you can read it, or run it yourself.
devs.title: For developers
devs.run.title: Run the server
devs.run.text: Locally with an API key, or with a double-click in Claude Desktop.
devs.build.title: Build with the API
devs.build.text: The code the assistant writes works as is in your site, with the SDK.
devs.build.keys: Use a read-only public key ({pk}) for public reads, and a secret key ({sk}), kept on the server, for writes.
